deities: Shri Chandreshwar (Lord Shiva as 'Lord of the Moon')
Shri Bhootnath (aspect of Shiva associated with spirits)

history.dynasty: Bhoja dynasty (titular deity; 4th-8th century); renovated by Kadambas (10th-11th century); present structure late 1600s
history.period: Ancient (claimed ~2500 years per Sanskrit inscription lore) to 17th century
history.summary: CSV town is WRONG: this temple is atop Chandranath Hill in Paroda, Quepem taluka, South Goa (~14 km from Margao) - not Margao. An ancient shrine of Shiva: local lore and a Sanskrit inscription claim a temple has stood here for nearly 2500 years, though only the rock-cut cavernous inner sanctum (hollowed from a boulder) is plausibly of great antiquity; the present Goan-style structure dates to the late 1600s. It was the titular deity of the Bhoja kings, who ruled South Goa till the 8th century and named their capital Chandrapur (today's Chandor) after him; Shiroda copper plates of Bhoja king Devarajah (c. 4th-5th century) mention Chandranath of Chandranath Hill near Chandor. Sources conflict on dates: the original is variously assigned to the Bhojas in the 3rd-4th, 4th-8th, or 6th-7th century, with Kadamba renovation in the 10th/11th century (c. 1050 CE). Chandreshwar is recorded as presiding deity of 22 villages. Legend holds that moonbeams falling on the self-manifested lingam on full-moon nights make water ooze from it. The hilltop (350 m) is reached by a metalled road or 300+ granite steps; entry is free.

name: Shri Chandreshwar Bhootnath Temple
town_description: Paroda is a village in Quepem taluka, South Goa, about 14 km from Margao on the road to Quepem. It lies at the foot of the wooded Chandranath Hill, topped by one of Goa's oldest Shiva temples, with sweeping views over the surrounding countryside.

travel.airport: Goa International Airport, Dabolim (~35 km) or Manohar International Airport, Mopa
travel.road: Metalled road runs up Chandranath Hill (scooter/car partway), or climb 300+ granite steps from the base; taxis and buses from Margao.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; early morning or evening for the hilltop views; full-moon nights draw devotees for the lingam legend.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:30 AM to 8:30 PM daily; entry free. Carry water if climbing the steps.
